answer: Physical Substrate Tie-In. Each identity must continuously submit fresh readings from a ferrous sensor coil embedded in hardware; the coil's magnetic noise is sampled and matched against prior traces. A fable told to a verifier does not reproduce the noise. Cloned hardware cannot replay readings because each sample mixes a quartz oscillator's drift with coil noise. Cost: an attacker must buy and physically run one full device per identity, plus a distinct coil, making bulk identity creation capital- and space-bound rather than free.
